name: Libertyville
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Libertyville, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Libertyville, IL: the Cook Park tree lighting, Dickens of a Holiday, the village Santa Parade and Cook Home open houses.
lede: Libertyville does Christmas downtown, around Cook Park on Milwaukee Avenue. The season opens with the village tree lighting on the Friday after Thanksgiving and builds to Dickens of a Holiday and a Santa Parade that rolls through the neighborhoods.
celebrates: The Village of Libertyville lights its holiday tree in Cook Park with carols, music and Santa arriving to help with the countdown, and MainStreet Libertyville turns the evening into a downtown holiday walk. A few weeks later comes Dickens of a Holiday, a downtown festival with photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus in his sleigh, a Children's Holiday Shoppe where kids ages 4 to 10 pick out gifts with help from Santa's elves, and a Victorian Tea. The Libertyville Historical Society opens the 1878 Ansel B. Cook Home for Victorian Christmas open houses, the village sends Santa through town on a parade with an online tracker map, and the recreation department hosts Donuts with Santa at the Crawford House.
lastyear: Christmas 2025 in Libertyville opened on November 28 with the tree lighting in Cook Park. Dickens of a Holiday marked 35 years downtown, the Daily Herald reported, and ran on Saturday, December 13, with Santa and Mrs. Claus in Cook Park, the Children's Holiday Shoppe and a Victorian Tea. The season had a movie twist too. The holiday film The Exes of Christmas Past, shot downtown that spring, began streaming in November, and a crew planned to return in mid December to film Christmas at the Zoo, with Cook Park set to appear on screen.
facts: The Ansel B. Cook Home, where the Historical Society holds its Christmas open houses, was built in 1878 as a summer home. After Emily Barrows Cook died in 1919, the house and grounds were given to the village for a library and park, and the house served as the town library from 1921 to 1968. Dickens of a Holiday turned 35 in 2025. And in The Exes of Christmas Past, downtown Libertyville plays a town called Mill Creek, with real shop names kept and local shopkeepers making cameos.
trains: Libertyville sits on Metra's Milwaukee District North line, which runs from Chicago Union Station to Fox Lake. The Libertyville station is at 200 W. Lake Street, and the Daily Herald notes the train stops right in the heart of downtown. A second stop, Prairie Crossing/Libertyville, is at 3001 Midlothian Road. Metra also runs decorated Holiday Trains with holiday characters on the MD-N line. Farther out, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway with Santa and his elves, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.

faq: When does Libertyville light its Christmas tree?

The Village of Libertyville holds its annual tree lighting in Cook Park on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Festivities start at 6:30 pm with music and singing, and Santa arrives to help with the countdown to light the Village Holiday Tree. MainStreet Libertyville pairs it with a downtown holiday walk, and a spot is set up for photos with Santa.
What is Dickens of a Holiday?

Dickens of a Holiday is MainStreet Libertyville's yearly downtown festival, which celebrated 35 years in 2025. Families can take photos with Santa and Mrs. Claus in his sleigh in Cook Park, kids can shop at the Children's Holiday Shoppe at the Libertyville Civic Center, and grownups can book a Victorian Tea. Food pantry donations are welcome at the Santa photos.
How does the Libertyville Santa Parade work?

The village's annual Santa Parade starts in the northwest corner of Libertyville and travels through the neighborhoods. The village posts the route and a Santa tracker map online so you can see when he is close. Bring blankets, cookies, hot chocolate and chairs, and if your street is on the route, park in the driveway so Santa's sleigh fits.
Can kids shop for gifts on their own in Libertyville?

Yes. At Dickens of a Holiday, the Children's Holiday Shoppe at the Libertyville Civic Center lets kids ages 4 to 10 shop for up to six gifts for loved ones, with help from Santa's elves. Patch reported in 2025 that adults stay out of the shop while children browse and that gifts are priced up to $6 each.
Can we take the train to Libertyville's Christmas events?

Yes. Libertyville is on Metra's Milwaukee District North line from Chicago Union Station, and the Libertyville station at 200 W. Lake Street stops right in the heart of downtown, where the tree lighting and Dickens of a Holiday take place. If you drive, free covered parking is available in the Church Street and Lake Street garages.
What is the Ansel B. Cook Home?

It is an 1878 house on Milwaukee Avenue that the Libertyville Historical Society runs as its headquarters and museum. Most rooms are furnished to show how the Cook family lived from 1878 to 1919, and the Museum Room upstairs shows items from Libertyville's past. It served as the town library from 1921 to 1968 and opens for Victorian Christmas open houses.
